name: Grading Calibration
title: Grading Calibration
answer: Grading calibration is the practice of teachers who share a course scoring the same samples of student work together and discussing their differences so that a student's grade does not depend on which teacher they happen to have. It matters because it builds consistency across a department and gives teachers a practical way to test whether an AI scoring tool agrees with their own professional judgment. No special product is required for the core practice.

sections.body: Calibration addresses the problem that teachers teaching the same course may grade the same work differently, which means a student's grade can depend on the teacher they are assigned rather than on the quality of their work. In calibration sessions, teachers score the same samples of student work and then discuss where their scores and reasoning diverged. The point is not to force everyone into identical numbers but to build shared understanding of standards through the discussion itself. Teachers learn from each other's reasoning and adjust their own judgments as a result. The book notes that no special product is needed to run this process.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: A department sets aside time for teachers of the same course to score a common set of student work samples, then meets to compare scores and talk through the differences. AI can help with the logistics, for example by organizing the samples or summarizing where teachers disagreed, but the discussion among teachers remains the place where calibration actually happens. The text does not give separate grade band variations, so the practice applies across the grade levels where a course is taught by more than one teacher. The same sessions double as a way to evaluate AI scoring features: teachers compare the tool's scores against their own calibrated scores on the same samples. Where the tool disagrees with calibrated teachers, it needs adjustment or should not be used.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no study, figure or formal evidence label for grading calibration. It presents the practice as a practical method any department can run rather than as a research finding, and it describes the comparison of AI scores against calibrated teacher scores as a practical test. This idea therefore rests on practice rather than research as stated in the book.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The book is clear that AI supports calibration without replacing it, and that the discussion among teachers is where calibration happens. The judgment about what a piece of student work deserves stays with the teachers, and the decision about whether an AI scoring tool is acceptable also stays with them. Where a tool disagrees with calibrated teachers, the text says it needs adjustment or should not be used, which places the final call in human hands. No product is required for the core practice, so adopting a tool is a separate decision a department makes rather than a condition of calibrating.
